subject: Third-party mapping & evidence handoff — scope clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@novamed.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: procure@novamed.com
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Evidence request: SIG/CAIQ + subprocessor roster for vendor review

Hi Lukas / Camila,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. As part of Novamed's procurement security review we need: 1) an up-to-date subprocessor roster broken out by function (kms, telemetry, hosting, analytics) with residency; 2) a completed SIG Lite / CAIQ matrix or answers to the attached SIG Q1 worksheet; 3) confirmation of key custody model for ephemeral keys used in inference.

Can you confirm you can deliver the roster and the completed worksheet by end of week (Friday, 2026-11-06)? If there are any items that require redaction or an NDA amendment before we can accept, flag them now and we'll escalate.

Attachments: novamed_sig_q1_request.pdf

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Senior Procurement Manager, Novamed Health
Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@novamed.com>
procure@novamed.com

---

(Please note: Novamed requires documentation evidencing SOC 2 Type II within the last 12 months; a link or PDF is fine.)

From: lukas_meyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@novamed.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence request: SIG/CAIQ + subprocessor roster for vendor review

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Summary of next steps from our side: 

- I'll deliver a CSV roster that categorizes subprocessors by function and region and flags any onshore/on-demand access controls (see attachment).
- Rishi will own the SIG/CAIQ answers and provide a SOC 2 Type II artifact link.
- Camila will gather any vendor attestation letters for onshore telemetry processors.

Target timeline: draft roster + SOC 2 link by EOD Thursday (2026-11-05), final answers/attachments by Friday if no additional clarifications are requested. If Novamed needs encrypted transfer, we can upload the artifacts to a secure Drive link or send via your secure FTP.

Attachment: redwood_subproc_inventory_v1.csv (columns: provider, service, function, residency, data_scope, contact, attestation)

A couple of clarifying Qs so we scope precisely:
1) Do you need the full contract/SoW numbers for each subprocessor or just the functional roster + attestation?
2) For KMS: do you need a keyflow diagram (how keys are generated/rotated) or just the key custody statement (Redwood manages ephemeral keys; customer-managed keys when requested via Private)?

If you'd like, happy to schedule a 20-min sync with Rishi and Camila tomorrow.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
lukas_meyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence request: SIG/CAIQ + subprocessor roster for vendor review

On Mon, 2026-11-02 at 11:03, lukas_meyer@redwood.com wrote:
> A couple of clarifying Qs so we scope precisely:

Quick answers for the record (will include in the SIG worksheet):
- Contract IDs: Novamed indicated they only need contract references for high-risk subprocessors (KMS, telemetry ingestion, model hosting). We'll supply contract IDs for those; others will be roster-only.
- KMS key custody: Redwood uses an ephemeral key model for hosted inference. Keys are generated per-tenant session and never stored persistently in our control plane; we do offer customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for Private deployments. I'll include a one-page keyflow diagram and the SOC 2 call-out on encryption.
- SOC2: attaching the current report (redacted) — filename: soc2-type2-redwood-2026.pdf (we host a copy and can provide an expiring S3 link).

I'll draft the SIG/CAIQ answers today and tag any items that require legal review (Pseudonymization details for analytics vendor, telemetry retention windows).

Rishi Malhotra
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: soc2-type2-redwood-2026.pdf

From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@novamed.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.com
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, procure@novamed.com
Date: 2026-11-04T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence request: SIG/CAIQ + subprocessor roster for vendor review

Lukas — this is great, thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed the roster draft and the SOC 2 link; two quick follow ups before we mark this closed on our side: 

1) Can you confirm the telemetry vendor (listed as "BluePulse Analytics") retains logs for up to 90 days and whether logs are pseudonymized at ingest? We flagged that for internal privacy.
2) Novamed will accept the SOC 2 Type II redacted PDF. Could you also provide a short note on your model update cadence and any controls you have for model rollbacks (we need this for operational resilience in our SIG review)?

If those two items are provided by EOD Thursday (2026-11-05) we can proceed to vendor approval. If not, we may need a brief legal-level redline on retention.

Thanks,
Elena

---

From: lukas_meyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@novamed.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-04T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence request: SIG/CAIQ + subprocessor roster for vendor review

Elena — confirmed.
- BluePulse Analytics: logs retained up to 90 days; ingest pipeline pseudonymizes PII fields by default (hashing + tokenization). Camila will attach the vendor attestation letter that contains retention and pseudonymization specifics.
- Model update cadence & rollback controls: Redwood runs scheduled weekly model patch windows for hosted catalog models; we maintain immutable model artifacts and an automated canary rollout pipeline (canary->50%->100%) with automatic rollback on regressions triggered by eval metrics or error rate thresholds. I'll include a short one-page operational note and a link to our rollout runbook.

We'll upload the two artifacts to the secure Drive link and send the access link to you within the hour. Please let us know if Novamed's legal team requires the vendor contract IDs for BluePulse and any other high-risk processors; we can provide those under an NDA or as redacted references.

Best,
Lukas

Attachments: redwood_subproc_inventory_v1.csv (previous), will follow: BluePulse_attestation.pdf, model_rollout_runbook_link
\n[Thread notes: attachments transferred to secure Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/redwood/novamed-subproc-evidence (access sent) ]
